title: Advancing Tool-Augmented Large Language Models via Meta-Verification and Reflection Learning

problem.claim: Tool-augmented large language models need reliable tool planning, invocation, and reflection to solve complex problems.

gap.claim: Existing models suffer from unreliable tool planning and invocation caused by low-quality instruction data and weak tool reflection caused by static imitation learning.

contributions.claim: Tool-MVR combines Multi-Agent Meta-Verification with Exploration-based Reflection Learning to support tool planning, invocation, and reflection.
Multi-Agent Meta-Verification constructs ToolBench-V, a high-quality tool-use instruction dataset.
Exploration-based Reflection Learning produces ToolBench-R, and the work proposes RefineToolBench for evaluating tool reflection capabilities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present Tool-MVR as novel, ToolBench-V as new, and RefineToolBench as the first benchmark specifically designed for tool reflection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Tool-MVR achieves state-of-the-art performance on StableToolBench, surpasses ToolLLM by 23.9% and GPT-4 by 15.3%, and reduces API calls by 31.4%.
The authors report strong generalization across unseen tools and scenarios.
The authors report a 58.9% error correction rate on RefineToolBench, compared with 9.1% for ToolLLM.

narrative_sequence.summary: Effective tool use is needed for LLM agents to solve complex problems.
Current models have unreliable tool planning and invocation and weak tool reflection.
Tool-MVR addresses the limitations through MAMV, EXPLORE, and fine-tuning on ToolBench-V and ToolBench-R.
The authors report performance, API-call, generalization, and error-correction results on StableToolBench and RefineToolBench.

source_observation.claim: The work combines validation of tool-use trajectories with feedback-driven reflection and correction.

interpretation.claim: Reliable tool use may benefit from jointly improving action quality before execution and error recovery after feedback.

application.claim: For tool-using agents, pair systematic validation data with learning data that represents error, reflection, and correction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination transfers to domains, tools, or model sizes beyond those evaluated.

source_observation.claim: The reported system reduces API calls while improving benchmark performance.

interpretation.claim: Improved tool reasoning may reduce unnecessary tool invocation as well as increase task success.

application.claim: Evaluate tool-augmented agents using both task outcomes and tool-use efficiency metrics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not explain how API-call reductions were measured or whether they involve trade-offs in latency or coverage.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the StableToolBench evaluation protocol, task composition, or statistical treatment.
The abstract does not provide training details, ablations, or implementation settings for MAMV and EXPLORE.
The abstract does not define the exact meaning of the reported percentage improvements or error-correction metric.
